sections.markdown:
## C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: deadlines, license ages and Standard versus REAL ID documents
Confusable pairs among deadlines, license types and identity documents, plus the REAL ID document steps that complete part C; each block ties to one handbook page, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec01-R01 | anchor: A01
An address change must be reported within one week of moving, while a legal name change gets two weeks; the two deadlines are easy to swap. [A01]
Why it matters: group deadlines; confusable address versus name change.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-R02 | anchor: A01
A new resident with a regular out-of-state license has 60 days to apply in New Jersey, a CDL holder has only 30 days, and a driver with a license from another country may drive on it for up to one year. [A01]
Why it matters: group deadlines; difficulty medium.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-R03 | anchor: A04
The basic automobile license requires age 18 and the probationary automobile license age 17, yet both list a permit age of 16. [A04]
Why it matters: group license types; confusable basic versus probationary.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-R04 | anchor: A05
A moped license starts at age 15, while an agricultural license is granted at 16 to 17 and is for farming only. [A05]
Why it matters: group license types; difficulty low.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-R05 | anchor: A03
The temporary paper license or ID lasts 30 days, while the mailed card itself is valid for four years. [A03]
Why it matters: group issuance; confusable temporary versus permanent card.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-R06 | anchor: A03
Most endorsements simply expire with the license, but a Hazmat endorsement must be retested every 2 years. [A03]
Why it matters: group endorsements; difficulty medium.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-R07 | anchor: A07
For a Standard license, address proofs such as a bank statement, a utility or credit card bill, or first class government mail may be up to one year old, and only one address proof is needed. [A07]
Why it matters: group documents; confusable Standard versus REAL ID address windows.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-R08 | anchor: A09
For REAL ID the address windows are tighter: a utility or credit card bill from the past 90 days, a bank or credit union statement from the past 60 days, or first class government mail from the past six months. [A09]
Why it matters: group documents; confusable Standard versus REAL ID address windows.
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-R09 | anchor: A07
A valid New Jersey license and a valid New Jersey vehicle registration both show an address, but they cannot be submitted together as address proofs. [A07]
Why it matters: group documents; difficulty medium.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-R10 | anchor: A08
A marriage or civil union certificate can be used only to prove a change of last name, while a divorce decree supports only a return to a previous name that it lists. [A08]
Why it matters: group name change; difficulty medium.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R11 | anchor: A08
An applicant who cannot get a Social Security number and has no ITIN may file an affidavit, which must be notarized or signed in front of an MVC agency employee. [A08]
Why it matters: group documents; difficulty low.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R12 | anchor: A08
If the Social Security Administration cannot verify the number given on the application, the applicant must bring a document showing the full name and full number, such as a Social Security card or a W-2 from the past year. [A08]
Why it matters: group documents; difficulty medium.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R13 | anchor: A08
The Standard document chart carries a separate note that CDL applicants must prove US citizenship or lawful permanent resident status. [A08]
Why it matters: group license types; confusable CDL versus basic license documents.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R14 | anchor: A09
REAL ID Step I is the two address proofs, Step II is one proof of the full Social Security number, and Step III is the six points from primary and secondary documents. [A09]
Why it matters: group REAL ID steps; difficulty medium.
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-R15 | anchor: A09
For REAL ID you select one and only one document from the primary list, for example an unexpired US passport or passport card, or a certified US birth certificate. [A09]
Why it matters: group REAL ID steps; difficulty low.
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-R16 | anchor: A09
Paper documents already used in REAL ID Steps I and II may also serve as secondary options in Step III when they appear on that list. [A09]
Why it matters: group REAL ID steps; difficulty high.
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-R17 | anchor: A10
In REAL ID Step III no more than two 1-point secondary documents may be used toward the six points. [A10]
Why it matters: group REAL ID steps; difficulty medium.
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-R18 | anchor: A10
An ATM or debit card and a bank statement cannot be submitted together, and financial details on documents may be blacked out. [A10]
Why it matters: group documents; difficulty low.
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-R19 | anchor: A10
On the REAL ID secondary list an unexpired standard photo license may come from New Jersey or any state, but an unexpired standard non-driver ID card counts only if New Jersey issued it. [A10]
Why it matters: group documents; confusable license versus non-driver ID origin.
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-R20 | anchor: A05
A license-chart footnote says a motorist who must return to a Licensing Center after one year to upgrade the license pays a prorated fee, usually $19.50 Standard or $29.00 REAL ID. [A05]
Why it matters: group license types; dynamic fee; footnote attachment held as debt in part D.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0010]
